title: Timeliner vs Gigxomi for Video Project Management
excerpt: Compare two video-focused platforms: Timeliner for video project management and Gigxomi for editing agency operations from enquiries to payouts.
seoDescription: Timeliner vs Gigxomi for video editing agencies: compare video project management with enquiries, teams, delivery, accounting, and payouts.
featuredImageAlt: Timeliner versus Gigxomi video project management guide
introduction: Timeliner and Gigxomi are closer competitors than general task tools because both speak to video work. Timeliner presents video project management capabilities around projects, tasks, feedback, client portals, team workload, and business administration. Gigxomi frames the problem as a business operating system for video editors, connecting messaging-led enquiries, agency roles, production, review, delivery, accounting, and payouts. Buyers should test the exact workflow depth rather than relying on category labels.
verdict: Choose Timeliner when its video-production project structure, client portal, task management, workload, and current commercial features match your service process. Choose Gigxomi when WhatsApp and Instagram client acquisition, explicit manager-editor routing, and a connected enquiry-to-payout path are decisive. Because both are specialist products, a hands-on pilot with the same client job is more valuable than a generic feature count.

sections.heading: Why specialist-versus-specialist needs a better test
paragraphs: When two products use the language of video production, broad checklist rows quickly become misleading. Both may mention projects, tasks, feedback, clients, and teams, yet implement ownership, permissions, versions, notifications, and financial state differently. The workflow details determine whether managers trust the system.

Prepare one standardized scenario before demonstrations. Include a new client, a recurring content package, two editors with different skills, a missed asset, an internal review, client revision, approved delivery, and a financial follow-up. Ask both vendors or trial environments to complete that sequence without changing the scenario.
bullets: Verify commercial capabilities for your region

sections.heading: Timeliner's stated strength: project-centered video work
paragraphs: Timeliner's official video project management material emphasizes keeping projects, tasks, feedback, clients, workload, and business activity together. That proposition is attractive for a production company that wants a video-native alternative to assembling a general project tool and a separate client portal.

The client portal and workload concepts deserve particular attention. Evaluate what clients can see, how feedback becomes accountable work, how capacity changes affect deadlines, and which reports operators actually receive. Current plan and payment details should be confirmed directly rather than inferred from old third-party reviews.

sections.heading: Gigxomi's stated strength: the messaging-to-payout chain
paragraphs: Gigxomi begins earlier in the client lifecycle. Many editing businesses sell through WhatsApp and Instagram, then manually convert conversations into projects. Its connected inbox direction and role-based routing aim to keep that customer context with managers and editors as work moves toward review and delivery.

The workflow also extends into accounting and payout visibility. That is valuable when an agency coordinates freelancers or editors whose compensation depends on real delivery state. Buyers should validate the current controls, payment provider flow, and permission boundaries with their actual operating policy.

sections.heading: Migration advice between video-native tools
paragraphs: Specialist systems often contain richer data than a spreadsheet export reveals. Inventory client identities, project hierarchy, tasks, comments, review references, files, team roles, workload assumptions, invoice or payment references, and audit history. Decide what must remain legally accessible and what only supports active delivery.

Move one service lane first, such as monthly short-form packages, and preserve stable project IDs in migration notes. Avoid redesigning the process during data transfer. After two complete cycles, compare manager time, editor clarity, client response, missed events, and finance reconciliation before selecting the permanent system.

sections.heading: A defensible final decision
paragraphs: Timeliner may be the better choice when its project-centered client portal and production planning closely match the agency's established process. Gigxomi may be better when social messaging is the commercial front door and the business needs explicit continuity through assignments and payouts.

Do not select either solely because it is marketed to video teams. Ask current, specific questions about storage, review behavior, permissions, notifications, integrations, mobile support, data export, payments, onboarding, and support. Record answers and verification dates so the decision remains auditable as products evolve.

decisionChecklist: Which platform completes your actual end-to-end scenario with fewer manual steps?
How do client portal permissions differ from connected inbox access?
Can managers reassign work without losing feedback and deadlines?
Which payment and payout functions are available in your country and plan?
How can all active and historical data be exported?
What onboarding and support response does the team require?
